summary: This project visualizes left behind hardware in an interactive way. It gives the younger generation a simpler way to view information about this left behind hardware. The webpage is a openly story-driven interactive map.  It shows the importance of some of this left behind hardware and what it has accomplished for the human race.
details:
Our project is an interactive 3D map that shows the hardware left behind by space missions. Its main goal is to make information about space exploration easier to understand and more interesting, especially for younger people.

Users can select a mission from a menu in the top-left corner of the page. A short summary then appears with the key facts, and users can open a longer, more detailed description if they want to know more. A 3D model of the hardware used in the mission, such as a rover or a drone, is also placed on the globe, which helps users see what the equipment actually looked like.

We built the project because the mission descriptions on NASA’s website are often very long, which can make them hard to read, particularly for younger readers or anyone who prefers shorter texts. We split the information into short, clear sections and combined them with interactive 3D models, so that learning about space is easier and more enjoyable.

Above all, we want young people to become curious about space. Learning about missions should be something you can explore yourself, not just a matter of reading long pages of text.

For the development, we used HTML and CSS for the structure and styling of the page, JavaScript for the interactive features, and Three.js to create and display the 3D models.
